questions.prompt: When is the Abita Springs Tourist Park closed to the public?
questions.answer: From dusk until dawn
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 416, adopted Oct. 18, 2011, repealed §§ 8-101—8-108, which pertained to recreation
               board and recreation facilities and derived from Ord. No. 103, §§ 1—8, adopted Dec.
               5, 1979.

The Abita Springs Tourist Park shall be closed to the public on each day from dusk
               until dawn.

"Dusk" shall be defined as approximately 30 minutes following sunset; "dawn" shall
               be defined as approximately 30 minutes prior to sunrise.

Exception to closure times may be granted when an individual or organization has properly
               scheduled, with the Mayor's Office of the Town of Abita Springs, an event in the park. (Ord. No. 417, 10-18-2011)

Failure to honor this article shall constitute trespassing. Violators shall be treated
               accordingly.

The Town of Abita Springs, including all land within the corporate limits, is hereby
               designated as a bird sanctuary. (Ord. No. 94, 8-5-75)

Every person is urged to conserve bird life through proper care and feeding and to
               protect birds from molestation, intimidation, traps, shooting, or robbing of nests.
               No person shall molest, trap, or shoot any bird, nor rob a bird nest. (Ord. No. 94, 8-5-75)

Any person violating any provision of this chapter shall, upon conviction, be fined
               or imprisoned as provided in section 1-108 of this Code. (Ord. No. 94, 8-5-75)

more than one-half of one percent alcohol

               malt, vinous, spirituous, alcoholic or intoxicating liquors, beer, porter, ale, stout,
               fruit juices, cider or wine. Beverages of high alcoholic content: Alcoholic beverages containing more than six (6) percent alcohol by volume. Beverages of low alcoholic content: Alcoholic beverages containing not more than six (6) percent alcohol by volume. Collector: The collector of revenue of Louisiana, or his duly authorized agents. questions.prompt: In Bossier Parish, which of these counts as an open container of alcohol?

A styrofoam or plastic cup, even if it has a lid on it
An unopened can in a cooler
A bottle whose tax stamp has never been broken
questions.answer: A styrofoam or plastic cup, even if it has a lid on it
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 22. State Law reference— Liquors, alcoholic beverages, R.S. 26:1 et seq.; size of containers of beverages of
               high alcoholic content, R.S. 26:351.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverage means any fluid or solid which is capable of being converted into fluid, suitable
               for human consumption, and containing more than one-half of one percent alcohol by
               volume, including malt, vinous, spirituous, alcoholic or intoxicating liquor, beer,
               porter, ale, stout, fruit juice, cider or wine. Beverages of high alcoholic content means alcoholic beverages containing more than six percent alcohol by volume. Beverages of low alcoholic content means alcoholic beverages containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume. Commissioner means the state commissioner of alcohol and tobacco control, who shall be the assistant
               secretary of alcohol and tobacco control in the state department of revenue, or his
               duly authorized agents. Open container means any container or receptacle of which the seal or stamp has been broken, or
               any container, bottle or can that has been opened subsequent to the filling of such
               container by the manufacturer, brewery or distillery of such alcoholic beverages.
               Alcoholic beverages contained in drinking glasses or cups, including plastic glasses
               and styrofoam cups, regardless of whether such container has a top fixed thereto,
               shall be deemed an open container. Private motor vehicle means any motorized vehicle which is not operating as a licensed passenger or contract
               carrier, including motorized two-wheel and three-wheel vehicles.…

questions.prompt: In Carencro, a drink is an alcoholic beverage if it has more than how much alcohol?
choices: One-half of one percent alcohol by volume
questions.answer: One-half of one percent alcohol by volume
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 18. State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, R.S. tit. 26; authority to regulate, R.S. 26:493; authority to
               levy local taxes, R.S. 26:491 et seq.; local license and permit fees authorized, R.S.
               26:74.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverages means any fluid or any solid capable of being converted into fluid, suitable for
               human consumption, and containing more than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume,
               including malt, vinous, spirituous, alcoholic or intoxicating liquors, beer, porter,
               ale, stout, fruit juices, cider or wine. Beverages of high alcoholic content means alcoholic beverages containing more than six percent alcohol by volume. Beverages of low alcoholic content means alcoholic beverages containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume. Handle means to sell, use, distribute, store, consume or otherwise handle. Malt beverages means beverages obtained by alcoholic fermentation or an infusion or concoction of
               barley or other grain, malt and hops in water, including, among other things, ale,
               beer, stout, porter and the like. Malt beverages are exclusive of all liquors whether
               they be defined as intoxicating or spirituous liquor or as alcoholic, vinous or malt
               liquors or however otherwise defined as liquors. Package house means a place where a person sells alcoholic beverages in closed containers, prepared
               for transportation and consumption off the premises. Retail dealer means every person who offers for sale, exposes for sale, has in his possession for
               sale or distribution, or sells alcoholic beverages of any quantity to persons…

The title of this part shall be known as the "Land Development Code of Franklin Parish,
               Louisiana." This part may also be cited as the "Land Development Code" or the "LDC."

Unless otherwise stated or where the context of the provision clearly shows a different
               intent, the provisions of chapter 1 shall apply to the chapters contained in this part.

Reasonable fees to offset the costs of administration of this part may be set by resolution
               of the police jury, from time to time, unless state law requires them to be established
               by ordinance.

(a) Where general requirements of a provision under the Code of General Ordinances or
               the Land Development Code conflict with a specific requirement of a provision under
               the Land Development Code, including but not limited to building and construction
               regulations, coastal zone management regulations, drainage and flood control, planning
               and development, and subdivision regulations, then the provision concerning the specific
               requirement under the Land Development Code shall prevail. (b) In the event that a provision or requirement under the Code of General Ordinances
               or the Land Development Code in any way conflicts with another provision or requirement
               under the Land Development Code, then the more stringent provision or requirement
               shall prevail.

               standards as the state uniform construction code, R.S. 40:1730.28 et seq.

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Liquors and alcoholic beverages generally, R.S. title 26.

By virtue of authority granted by Act 190 of the Louisiana Legislature of 1946, there
               is hereby levied, in addition to all other excise, license or privilege taxes presently
               imposed, a tax on all beer, porter, ale, fruit juices and/or wine having an alcoholic
               content of not less than one-half of one (1) per cent or more than six (6) per cent,
               by volume, of one dollar and fifty cents ($1.50) per standard barrel of thirty-one
               (31) gallons, or any like rate of any other quantity, or for the fractional parts
               of such barrel sold for consumption in the Parish of Iberville, within the meaning
               and intent of the provisions of Act 190 of the Louisiana Legislature of 1946. (Ord. of 9-10-46; Ord. of 8-4-81) Cross reference— Taxation generally, ch. 23 .

The tax levied by section 2-1 shall be collected by any and all Louisiana wholesale dealers from their vendees
               purchasing for consumption in the Parish of Iberville on each sale and shall be remitted
               by said wholesale dealers to the collector of revenue of the State of Louisiana, for
               each month, on or before the twentieth day of each succeeding month, respectively,
               all in accordance with rules and regulations promulgated by the collector of revenue

Historical and statutory note— The 1832 act established the town of Jackson as an incorporated body. The 1926 amendment
            added the provisions contained in Section 8 . The 1977 amendment added the provisions contained in Section 7 . The Charter of the Town of Jackson was amended on three other occasions, as cited
            above. The 1834 amendment authorized the Town to enact a property tax and a tax on
            those engaged in certain occupations. This amendment has been superseded by the state's
            enactment of a general statewide property tax law, La. Constitution art. 7, Sec. 23
            and La. R.S. 47:1705 et seq. and the state occupational license tax law, La. R.S.
            47:341 et seq. Both state statutes cited authorize the Town to levy the types of taxes
            described. ;le=2;The 1857 amendment changed the date for annual elections for trustees to the
            first Monday in September. Section 3 originally provided for one year terms for the
            Mayor and Trustees, with elections on the first Monday in July. These provisions have
            been superseded by the state election law, La. R.S. 18:402(C), now providing for election
            of municipal officers for terms of four years, with primary elections to be held on
            the first Saturday in April of the election year, and with a general election to be
            held on the sixth Saturday following the primary election. General state legislation
            supersedes the rights and powers of a municipality regarding the subject of the state
            legislation. State ex rel. Kemp v. City of Baton Rouge, 215 La. 315, 40 So. 2d 477

questions.prompt: Who did the City of Jeanerette name as its tourist promotion agency?
questions.answer: The Jeanerette Chamber of Commerce
questions.excerpt:
The Jeanerette Chamber of Commerce is hereby designated and shall hereafter be known
               as the tourist promotion agency for the City of Jeanerette. (Ord. No. 1-1982, § 1, 3-8-82)

The Jeanerette Chamber of Commerce, functioning in its capacity as a tourist promotion
               agency, is hereby authorized to make application to and receive grants from or contract
               with the Louisiana Tourist Development Commission for tourism-related projects in
               and for the City of Jeanerette, and is further authorized to contract with any agency,
               board or commission of federal, state or local government for the purpose of promoting
               tourism or related projects. (Ord. No. 1-1982, § 1, 3-8-82)

The tourist promotion agency, as designated hereinabove, shall have full authority
               to contract for its own account in connection with tourism-related projects; provided,
               however, that no commitment for the expenditure of any public funds shall be made
               by said agency on behalf of the City of Jeanerette without specific prior approval
               of the mayor and board of aldermen of the City of Jeanerette. (Ord. No. 1-1982, § 1, 3-8-82)

A parks and recreation commission for the City of Jeanerette is hereby created to
               be known as the Jeanerette Parks and Recreation Commission (PARC). (Ord. No. 2-1984, § 1, 6-11-84)

               be citizens and residents of the City of Jeanerette and who shall serve without compensation.

               shall be ex officio members of the board in addition to the nine (9) members before
               mentioned. The members of the board shall be appointed by the mayor with the concurrence

questions.excerpt:
The title of this part shall be known as the "Land Development Code of LaSalle Parish,
               Louisiana." This part may also be cited as the "Land Development Code" or the "LDC."

Unless otherwise stated or where the context of the provision clearly shows a different
               intent, the provisions of chapter 1 under part I, Code of General Ordinances, shall apply to the chapters contained in
               this part.

Reasonable fees to offset the costs of administration of this part may be set by resolution
               of the police jury, from time to time, unless state law requires them to be established
               by ordinance.

(a) Where general requirements of a provision under the Code of General Ordinances or
               the Land Development Code conflict with a specific requirement of a provision under
               the Land Development Code, including, but not limited to, airport hazard zoning, building
               and construction regulations, floods, planning and zoning, and subdivision regulations,
               then the provision concerning the specific requirement under the Land Development
               Code shall prevail. (b) In the event that a provision or requirement under the Code of General Ordinances
               or the Land Development Code in any way conflicts with another provision or requirement
               under the Land Development Code, then the more stringent provision or requirement
               shall prevail.

questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Parish parks, R.S. 33:4622.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Commercial means, as a business, or for profit, or where a fee or purse is paid to contestants,
               or where a charge is made for witnessing the event. Motor-powered vehicle means any vehicle or contrivance having two or more wheels and propelled by a motor
               using gasoline or any other combustible liquid fuel. Sport park means any lot, parcel or tract of land, enclosed or otherwise, used for racing or
               competitive sporting events as a business for profit. (Code 1979, § 9-16; Ord. No. 353, § 1, 3-27-1973)

Any person who desires to create, construct, maintain or operate a sport park as a
               business for profit shall first submit to the parish police jury a complete set of
               plans and specifications of any such sport park to be constructed, maintained or operated
               in the parish and receive therefrom the approval of the police jury of such plans
               and specifications. (Code 1979, § 9-17; Ord. No. 353, § 2, 3-27-1973)

No sport park where motor-powered vehicles are used shall be constructed, maintained
               or operated as a business for profit without its owner and/or operator first obtaining
               the approval of all landowners and tenants owning property within 1,000 yards of its
               perimeter. No sport park where motor-powered vehicles are not used shall be constructed,
               maintained or operated as a business for profit without its owner and/or operator
               first obtaining the approval of all landowners, and tenants owning property within
               300 yards of its perimeter. (Code 1979, § 9-18; Ord. No. 353, § 3, 3-27-1973)

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 22; health, sanitation, and property standards, ch. 38; taxation, ch. 82. State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, R.S. 26:1 et seq.; local regulatory ordinances, R.S. 26:493.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverages means any fluid, or any solid capable of being converted into fluid, suitable for
               human consumption and containing more than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume,
               including malt, vinous, spirituous, alcoholic or intoxicating liquors, beer, porter,

               dead animals or fowls, industrial waste or refuse or any other substance which may

               with section 1-21 of this Code. (Ord. of 7-10-62)

Owners or occupants of all dwelling and business places where garbage, paper, trash,
               etc., accumulates are hereby required to provide and have on hand at least one garbage
               can. If the street commissioner of the city deems that more than one garbage can is
               necessary to adequately take care of the garbage, then a sufficient number shall be
               provided. (Ord. of 3-12-57, § 2)

As used in this article, the term "garbage can" shall mean any can manufactured for
               the purpose of holding garbage. No garbage can shall have a capacity of less than ten gallons nor more than 35 gallons.
               Each garbage can shall be provided with a lid which will at all times fit tightly
               and exclude rain water and flies. All garbage cans shall be of metal and of a type
               approved by the state department of health. The use of lard cans, tubs or containers
               other than regular garbage cans, for the purpose of holding garbage, is hereby prohibited. (Ord. of 3-12-57, § 1)

It shall be unlawful for any person to be guilty of cruelty to any animal. Cruelty to animals is the intentional or criminally negligent mistreatment of any
               animal by any act or omission whereby unjustifiable physical pain, suffering or death
               is caused or permitted upon such animal. (Code 1976, § 11-1060) State Law reference— Cruelty to animals, R.S. 14:102, 14:102.1.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person, corporation, companies, or any entity whatsoever
               to own or harbor the following animals within the corporate limits of the town: (1) Hogs, pigs, or any animal of the swine family; (2) Cows or any animals of the cow kind; (3) Sheep, goats, peacocks, ducks, or geese; and, (4) Horses and mules, or any animal of the horse and mule kind. (b) Any violation of this section by any entity shall subject said person, corporation
               or entity to a fine of not more than fifty dollars ($50.00) per day for each day of
               the violation and/or imprisonment for not more than thirty (30) days or both. (c) Any animals found in violation of this section may be taken in charge of by any officer

               foster care home and there detained until the owner thereof shall come forward and

               et seq.; Airport Authorities Law, R.S. 2:601 et seq.

There is hereby established a zoned area consisting of all of that territory adjacent
               to the Hart Airport and located within 2,500 feet of said airport. (Code 1992, app. A, § 1)

There is hereby established in said zoned area an obstruction line located as follows:
               the said obstruction line shall begin at the ground at the boundary line of said airport
               and shall extend upward and outward in a straight line, so that when it reaches the
               outer boundary of said zoned area, it shall be 100 feet above the ground. (Code 1992, app. A, § 2)

After the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived, no person
               shall build or construct any building or other structure in said zoned area which
               shall rise above said obstruction line. (Code 1992, app. A, § 3)

No person shall maintain any building or other structure in said zoned area which
               shall rise above said obstruction line and which shall have been constructed after
               the effective date of the ordinance from which this chapter is derived. (Code 1992, app. A, § 4)

No person shall maintain any tree, bush or shrub in said zoned area which rises above
               said obstruction line. (Code 1992, app. A, § 5)

Any person who shall violate any of the provisions of this chapter shall be guilty
               of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by a fine not exceeding
…

questions.prompt: In Slidell, what counts as an alcoholic beverage?

Any drink with more than six percent alcohol
questions.answer: A drink with more than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 8; dangerous weapons prohibited on premises of alcoholic beverage
               outlets, § 11-192; sale of alcoholic beverages in parks, § 19-7; consumption of alcoholic beverages by occupants of motor vehicles, § 27-4. State Law reference— Local alcoholic beverage permits, R.S. 26:74, 26:274; local taxation and regulation,

               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverages means any fluid or any solid capable of being converted into fluid, suitable for
               human consumption, and containing more than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume,
               including malt, vinous, spirituous, alcoholic or intoxicating liquors, beer, porter,
               ale, stout fruit juices, cider or wine. Beverages of high alcohol content or high content alcoholic beverages means alcoholic beverages containing more than six percent alcohol by volume. questions.prompt: In Sorrento, bars, taverns, and lounges that sell alcohol for drinking on site must stay closed and cannot serve drinks of any kind (even non-alcoholic) during which hours?
questions.answer: 12:00 midnight to 6:00 a.m.
questions.excerpt:
For purposes of this chapter, the following terms have the respective meanings ascribed
               to them in this section, unless a different meaning clearly appears from the context: Alcoholic beverages means any fluid or solid capable of being converted into fluid, suitable for human
               consumption and containing more than one-half of one percent alcohol by volume. Beverages of high alcoholic content means alcoholic beverages containing more than six percent alcohol by volume. Beverages of low alcoholic content means alcoholic beverages containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume.

(a) It shall be unlawful under the provisions of this chapter for the proprietor, owner,
               agent, or employees of any barroom, club, tavern, lounge, or other establishment where
               alcoholic beverages are sold and consumed on the premises to serve drinks of any kind,
               whether alcoholic content or not, in or on the premises during the hours between 12:00
               midnight and 6:00 a.m., during which hours said establishment shall remain closed. (b) Exception for certain restaurants. Notwithstanding the previous paragraph, any restaurant establishment with a valid
               permit or license to sell alcoholic beverages from the state office of alcohol and
               tobacco control, and which serves food as its primary source of business, may serve
               alcoholic/nonalcoholic beverages approved by said permit past 12:00 midnight on Thursday,
               Friday, and Saturday nights only until 2:00 a.m. the following mornings. (c) Violations of this section shall be punished by a fine of not less than $250.00 or
               more than $500.00, imprisonment not exceeding 60 days, or both. In addition, third
               offenders shall have their licenses suspended for 30 days, and reinstatement must
               have approval of the town council. (Code 1977, § 7-12; Ord. No. 06-18, § 1,…

Horses, mules, asses, cattle, swine, sheep, and goats are hereby prohibited from roaming
               at large on the public highways of the Second and Sixth Wards of the Parish of St.
               Helena, State of Louisiana. (Ord. of 8-4-1965; Ord. of 3-30-1974) Editor's note— The ordinances indicated in the source note were adopted following special elections
               held in Wards Two and Six, respectively, in accordance with R.S. 3:3001 et seq. R.S.
               3:3001 et seq. grant every parish in the state the right, by local option election,
               to prohibit livestock at large on public highways in particular wards. These provisions
               of state law also set forth procedures for the impoundment, advertisement, and sale
               of unredeemed livestock and are included herein as sections 4-3—4-8 for the convenience
               of the user. State Law reference— Authority of police juries to adopt stock ordinances without the use of the local
               option election, R.S. 33:1236(5); state prohibition against livestock roaming on state
               maintained highways, see R.S. 3:2801 et seq.

               parish, of Ward One and Ward Three of St. Helena Parish, Louisiana.…

questions.prompt: In St. James Parish, a Class A-general liquor permit for drinks over 6 percent alcohol requires the business to get at least what share of its retail sales income from alcohol served for drinking on the premises?
questions.answer: At least 75 percent
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Alcoholic beverages, R.S. title 26.

(a) Liquor permits. There shall be issued the following types of liquor permits to businesses dealing
               in beverages of high alcoholic content of more than six percent by volume: (1) Permit classifications. a. Class A-general. 1. A Class A-general retail permit shall be issued only to a retail outlet where beverage
               alcohol is sold on the premises for consumption on the premises by paying customers.
               Such an establishment must be equipped with a permanent wet bar equipped with a nonmovable
               sink and a backbar or similar equipment for public display and to inform the public
               of brands and flavors offered for sale. 2. A Class A-general retail establishment shall be staffed by a bartender whose primary
               duty is to open and/or prepare beverage alcohol products for consumption on the premises
               by paying customers, or prepared with an appropriate lid or cover on the container
               for take-out service. Such an establishment must meet all state and parish zoning
               requirements as set forth by the state and the parish. 3. A Class A-general retail permit holder must derive at least 75 percent of its total
               retail sales income from the sale of beverage alcohol for consumption on the premises. 4. A Class A-general retail permit shall be issued only to an establishment where the
               state law provides that no person under the age of 18 years is allowed on the premises
               except as provided in R.S. 26:90(A)(8)(a). 5. Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (b)(1)a.1 through 4 of this section,
               the council may issue a Class A-general liquor permit to any bona fide commercial
               film theater that had a Class A liquor permit on January 1, 1994. 6. Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (b)(1)a.1 through 5…
